title: Derived coinduction is right adjoint to restriction of scalars
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $U:D(B)\to D(R)$ be restriction of scalars on the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $K\in D(R)$ choose a K-injective representative $I$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and put $C_B(K)=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$ with $B$-action $(b\cdot h)(b')=h(b'b)$. This construction, with the canonical comparisons between K-injective representatives, is independent of the choices and defines a functor $C_B:D(R)\to D(B)$ right adjoint to $U$. Its underlying $R$-object is canonically $U C_B(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B[0],K)$. The counit $U C_B(K)\to K$ is represented by evaluation $h\mapsto h(1)$ into $I$. The functor $U$ is conservative: a morphism in $D(B)$ is an isomorphism if its restriction is an isomorphism in $D(R)$. No boundedness or flatness assumption on the ring map or on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), section Trivial duality for a ring map, lines 2198-2248. The counit is the ordinary Hom/restriction counit degreewise; restriction reflects acyclicity because kernels, images and cohomology are unchanged as underlying modules.

proof.text: View ordinary modules over $R$ as modules on the one-object ringed site of $R$. The K-injective-resolution existence theorem [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies functorial K-injective replacements. Apply the derived internal-Hom construction [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to $B[0]$ and a representative $I$ of $K$: it gives the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$ and its derived object. The comparison theorem [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] shows that changing either the representative or the K-injective replacement by a quasi-isomorphism induces a quasi-isomorphism of these Hom complexes. Therefore the displayed construction is independent of choices and is functorial on $D(R)$.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71; construction of RHom by a K-injective representative

proof.text: Right multiplication in $B$ defines the action $(b\cdot h)(b')=h(b'b)$. Associativity and the unit law follow from multiplication in $B$, and the action commutes with the Hom differential because $B[0]$ has degree zero and the action is by precomposition with an $R$-linear map. Forgetting this action leaves exactly the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$, so the underlying $R$-object is canonically $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B[0],K)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 0A71, proof: the restriction of RHom(B,K) is represented by Hom(B,I)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] with $P=R$ and $A=B$. For $X\in D(B)$ and $K\in D(R)$ it gives a natural internal-Hom isomorphism $$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,C_B(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(UX,K),$$ induced by evaluation at $1$ with inverse $g\mapsto(x\mapsto[b\mapsto g(bx)])$. On the one-object ringed site, [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies $H^0$ of each derived internal Hom with the corresponding Hom-set in the derived category. Taking $H^0$ therefore yields the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(X,C_B(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(UX,K)$, so $C_B$ is right adjoint to $U$.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71, derived coinduction adjunction; one-object specialization

proof.text: Under the bijection in Step 3, the identity of $C_B(K)$ is sent to evaluation at $1$: the evaluation formula in [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] sends a Hom-complex map $f$ to $x\mapsto f(x)(1)$, and setting $X=C_B(K)$ and $f=1$ gives $h\mapsto h(1)$. Thus the adjunction counit $U C_B(K)\to K$ is represented by evaluation at $1$.

Restriction of scalars changes only the module action, so it is exact and the cohomology of $Uf$ is the underlying $R$-linear map of the cohomology of $f$. An underlying module map is an isomorphism exactly when the same map with its additional $B$-linearity is an isomorphism. Hence, if $Uf$ is an isomorphism, every $H^n(f)$ is an isomorphism; the criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] then makes $f$ an isomorphism in $D(B)$. This proves that $U$ is conservative (the converse implication is immediate from functoriality).
